root.name: Mikenas Defense: Cannstatter Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nc6 2. c4 e5 3. d5 Nd4

overview: After 1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nd4 Black plants a knight on d4 and aims for ...Nf5 or ...Bb4+; White takes space with e3 and Nc3 and gains time by chasing the knight. The line is rarely played and I am not sure of the best handling.

white_ideas.idea: Chase the d4 knight with e3
Develop with Nc3 and Nf3, keeping the space edge
Use the c4/d5 chain to restrict Black

black_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight to f5 with ...Nf5

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on c4 and d5 against a Black pawn on e5, with the d-pawn locked

character.notes: A quiet space-gain for White against awkward knight play; Black is passive rather than tactical.

gambit.notes: No material is given on purpose in the main line.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious for Black; White gains time and space.

structure.notes: Pawns on d5/e5 lock the centre.

approach.notes: Rare; strong players seldom choose 1...Nc6 against 1.d4.

level.notes: Little theory but not a recommended repertoire.

character.reason: No forcing play, but Black is a little offside.

soundness.reason: Black loses time with the knight on d4.
